newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean union leader to defy prosecution summons.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean union leader to defy prosecution summons.

text.p: South Korea's outlawed union body will ignore a prosecution summons to about 20 leaders to appear for questioning over strikes sweeping the nation, its leader said on Monday.
"We will not respond to the prosecution summons," Kwon Young-kil, president of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, told a news conference. He added that no summons had yet been delivered.

Kwon renewed a threat to bring out public sector workers at hospitals, broadcasters and medical insurance firms unless President Kim Young-sam announced a repeal of a controversial labour law at a news conference scheduled for Tuesday.
Strikes have crippled much of South Korean industry since the law was rammed through parliament on December 26.
Kwon accused the government of trying to divert public attention from the industrial unrest by provoking a showdown between his militant labour body and public prosecutors.
"Despite the government's strong response we will push on with our strikes and we won't back down," Kwon said.
